caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 80 of 2010.
lawyer:
Mansur Habib, Advocate, instructed by Md Muzibar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
None Represented—For Respondents.
parties:
Shah Sekandar Molla ----- Petitioner 
VS.
New Sagurnal Tea Co and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Muzammel Hossain J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 11-10-2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2009 making the Rule absolute and thereby transferred the Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 pending in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

 2. The present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 on 22-9-2005 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar impleading the respondents as defendants for realization of Taka 1,83,84,152 stating, inter alia, that on 18-3-2002 a contact was executed and signed by the defendant No. 2 respondent No. 2 and the plaintiff-petitioner for selling of 1.50 lakh cubic feet of timber worth Taka 3,00,00,000 and in lieu thereof the defendants had received Taka 20,00,000 as security money from the plaintiff-petitioner. Subsequently, the plaintiff-petitioner allegedly spent at least Taka 20,00,000 for obtaining permission from the government for cutting, carrying and selling timbers. On 28-2-05 the plaintiff again claimed to have spent Taka 7,00,000 and Taka 20,00,000 for the said purpose and in the similar manner the plaintiff had claimed to have spent Taka 82,84,952. It has been alleged that on 8-6-04 at about 11-00 hours the defendant Nos. 2-4 respondent Nos. 2-4 and some other persons called on the plaintiff-petitioner at their office situated at Dhaka directing him not to demand any money from them and ultimately denied his claim. It has further been alleged that the defendants are trying to sell the timbers to other persons. Finding no other alternative the plaintiff-petitioner filed complaint Petition Case No. 1349 of 2004 through the constituted attorney before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 10-6-04 which was ultimately registered as Ramna Police Station Case No. 57(9)04 corresponding to GR No. 896 of 2004. The Investigating Officer after completion of investigation submitted police report for the alleged commission of the offence punishable under sections 406, 420 and 506 of the Penal Code in support of the cause of action of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005. Then charge was framed against the defendants-respondents under sections 406, 420 and 506 of the Penal Code. Challenging the impugned proceedings the defendants-respondents moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15235 of 2005 in which Rule was issued and all further proceedings of the said GR Case was stayed. A Division Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 12-9-2007 discharged the Rule with a direction upon the learned Magistrate to stay all further proceedings of the said GR case till disposal of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 pending before the Court of joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar. It has further been contended that the plaintiff had so far collected 1,41,160 cubic feet of timbers worth about Taka 67,94,200 and that the remaining 1,30,884 cubic feet of timbers were allegedly lying in the said tea garden of the defendants-respondents. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 respondents preferred Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2009 under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2009 before the High Court Division for transfer of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 from the Court of Joint District Judge; 1st Court, Moulvibazar to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for analogous hearing with Money Suit No. 21 of 2006. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 11-10-2009 made the Rule absolute transferring the Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 from the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Moulvibazar to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for analogous hearing with Money Suit No. 21 of 2006. 

 6. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the this case in its true perspective as a result of which there has been serious miscarriage of justice since the place of occurrence with regard to Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 instituted by the plaintiff-petitioner is at Moulvibazar whereas Money Suit No. 21 of 2006 filed by the defendant No. 2. New Sagurnal Tea Co represented by its Chairman is shown to have been in Dhaka and that the evidence of PW 1 in Money Suit No. 2 of 2006 has some time ago been recorded by the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar for doing effective and complete justice, the earlier suit should not be transferred from Moulvibazar to Dhaka and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He then submits that all the PWs of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 filed by the plaintiff-petitioner are frightened to depose at Dhaka since the activists of the defendants-respondents have created a panicky situation to harass and humiliate them and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with for ends of justice. 

 7. We have heard Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, perused the leave petition, impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and all other connected papers on record. Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure confers a general power upon the High Court Division and the District Judge to transfer, withdraw suits, appeals and other proceedings at any stages on the application of the parties or sue motu. The power under section 24 is discretionary in nature which must be exercised judiciously not capriciously or authority but for "substantial reasons" or "good grounds" based on the facts and circumstances of each case. Section 24 does not stipulate any condition for transfer of a case from one Court to another. There is no exhaustive list of "good grounds" or "sufficient grounds" for transferring a case, suit or appeal from one Court to another. But the Court is required to exercise its discretion judiciously upon some established principles for "good grounds" or "sufficient grounds" some of which are, namely balance of convenience of the parties, bias in a judge causing reasonable apprehension of not getting justice, embarrassment of the Court, environment not congenial to fair trial, common question of law and facts raised in the suits, a question of interpretation of law and constitution of far-reaching importance is involved, intricate and complicated question of law of general public importance and for avoiding failure of justice, possibility of conflicting decisions and multiplicity of proceedings or any other cogent ground depending on the facts and circumstances of the case which can justify transfer of a case for ensuring equality and justice to both the parties of the suits. 

 8. An application for transfer in the High Court Division being an independent original proceeding within the meaning of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure should generally be self-contained and supported by a properly sworn affidavit. The plaintiff as the arbiter litis has the right to choose his forum but the Court should be very reluctant to interfere with his right unless the petitioner makes out a case for transfer and the application has been made bonafide. It has been judicially established in a number of cases that transfer of a case from one Court to another should not be lightly dealt with because it is a serious matter which indirectly casts a doubt on the integrity of competency of the learned judge from whom the matter is transferred. In transferring a case the paramount consideration of the Court would be to meet the ends of justice. The burden verily lies upon the party who is seeking transfer of a case substantiating good, sufficient or weighty grounds which are based on established principles for transfer of a case from one Court to another competent Court which is subordinate to the High Court Division or to the Court of District Judge or to the High Court Division as the case may be. 

 9. On perusal of the petition under section 24 of the Code of -Civil Procedure and the plaint of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 it transpires that admittedly the contract dated 18-3-2002 between the petitioner and the respondent was entered into for sale and purchase of 150 lakh cft timber in Dhaka and both the parties and their witnesses reside in Dhaka and the cause of action of both the Money Suit for alleged breach of contract dated 18-3-2002 arose in Dhaka and both the parties voluntarily reside, carry on business and personally work for gain in Dhaka and the present petitioner as the complainant filed a petition of complaint being No. 1349 of 2004 before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka which was subsequently registered as Ramna Police Station Case No. 57 dated 18-9-2004 against the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and others as accused persons under sections 406, 420 and 506 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR Case No. 896 of 2004 basing on the same cause of action of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 and from the police report it transpires that all the witnesses of the present petitioner of the GR case also hail from Dhaka. Since the Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 instituted at the instance of the present petitioner for compensation for alleged breach of contract before the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar and Money Suit No. 21 of 2006 instituted at he instance of the respondent for compensation for alleged breach of contract against the petitioner and these two suits have arisen out of the same subject matter i.e. the contract dated 18-3-2002 signed in Dhaka, both the contending parties actually reside and carry on business and personally work for gain in Dhaka and the cause of action of both the suits arose in Dhaka. On the self same allegation and cause of action a criminal case being Ramna Police Station Case No. 57 dated 18-9-2004 under sections 406, 420 and 506 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR Case No. 896 of 2004 basing more or less on the same cause of action of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 has arisen and from the police report it also transpires that all the witnesses also bailed from Dhaka. 

 10. In the instant case both the money suits arose from the self same subject matter i.e. the contract dated 18-3-2002 entered into between the same parties and both the parties alleging breach of contract and claiming compensation against each other for alleged breach of contract filed the aforesaid two Money Suits. In this context it would be pertinent to refer to the decision of the case of Integrated Services Limited vs Khaleda Rahman reported in 5 BLC (AD) 69 wherein Appellate Division held that as both the suits are over the self same subject matter the High Court Division can mote exercise its authority under section 24 CPC and withdraw the earlier suit and transfer it to be tried along with the later suit analogously by the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka as has been correctly found by the High Court Division. In the case of Abdul Latif Chowdhury vs Md Noor Hossain reported in 2 MLR (AD) 298 the Appellate Division held that the purpose of holding analogous trial or hearing of different suits-arising out of same properties by a single Court of competent jurisdiction is to avoid conflicting decisions with respect to the same property. Even in the case the suit are different for different properties but arising out of land of same plot, all the suits relating to the suit property, should be tried by one Court. Evidence should be taken separately in each suit and those different suits should be disposed of by separate judgments by the same Court. While commenting on the discretionary power of transfer of a suit or proceeding and the ground for transfer the Supreme Court of India in the case of Indian Overseas Bank, Madras vs Chemical Construction Co. and others reported in AIR 1979 SC 1514 at page 1516 observed as under: 

 "Although the exercise of this discretionary power cannot be imprisoned within the strait-jacket of any cast iron formula uniformly applicable to all situations yet, certain broad proposition as to what may constitute a ground for transfer can be deduced from judicial decisions. One of them is that where two suits raising common questions of facts and laws between parties common to both the suits, are pending in two different Courts, it is generally in the interest of justice to transfor one of those suits to the other forum to be tried by the same Court, with consequent avoidance of multiplicity in the trial of the same issues and the risk of conflicting decisions thereon. The instant case falls squarely within this category." 

 11. From the pleadings of the parties of two money suits before us it transpires that common question of law and fact is involved in the matter. In this context, reference may be made to the decision of the case of Saroj vs Girija, AIR 1926 Cal 326 wherein it has been held that if two cases raise common question of law and fact one case should be transferred to have both the cases heard together in the same Court by the same Judge, In the present case these two money suits also raise common questions of fact and law and the decisions to be taken in these two Money Suits seem to be interdependent as discussed above. According to the decision of the case of Purna Chandra vs Samantha, AIR 1953 Orissa 46 where there are two suits in different Court raising common question of fact and law and the decisions in which are interdependent, the requirement of justice is that they should be tried together in the same Court by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and conflict of decisions. 

 12. In order to transfer a suit the convenience which is to be taken into consideration by the Court is the convenience of both the parties not any one of them. But the convenience of the parties depends on the facts and circumstances of each case. If the suit is instituted by the plaintiff in a Court from which transfer is sought for to prevent abuse of the process of the Court the preponderance of convenience should be the guiding factor in transferring a suit. We find that Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 was instituted in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar in 2005 and the Money Suit No. 21 of 2006 was subsequently preferred in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in 2006. The plaintiffs in these two money suits made out their respective cases having their causes of action at Moulvibazar and Dhaka respectively. At this stage we refrain from expressing our views on the merits of these two suits. Be that as it may, these two money suits were filed before the competent Courts having jurisdiction to try these suits. We are of the view that the word "competent" in section 24 refers to "pecuniary jurisdiction" only and not "territorial jurisdiction". In the instant case according to the respective plaintiffs both the suits were filed before the Courts of Joint District Judge having both pecuniary and territorial jurisdictions to try these suits. When a suit for the Court of Joint District Judge, Moulvibazar is transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka which being the transferee Court is competent to try the Suit of the Court of Joint District Judges, Moulvibazar since the transferee Court exercises all the powers of the Court from which the suit has been transferred. 

 13. The High Court Division on perusal of the plaints of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 and Money Suit No. 21 of 2006 rightly found that both the contending parties admittedly hail from Dhaka and the causes of action for instituting these two suits for alleged breach of contract dated 18-3-2002 also arose in Dhaka. It has also been noticed by the High Court Division that the present petitioner as the complainant filed petition of complaint being No. 1349 of 2004 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under sections 406 and 506 of the Penal Code against the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and others as the accused persons which was recorded as GR Case No. 896 of 2004 basing on the same cause of action of Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 and from the police report it transpires that all the witnesses of the present petitioner of GR Case who are also common witnesses in the aforesaid suits also hail from Dhaka. Having considered the facts and circumstances of these two money suits the High Court Division rightly held that for the convenience of both the contending parties and also to avoid conflicting decisions and abuse of the process of the Court Money Suit No. 2 of 2005 preferred at the instance of the petitioner in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar be transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka to be tried analogously with Money Suit No. 21 of 2006 instituted by the present respondent No. 1.
